parsed.explanation: Combined regime is hostile and universal. Federal rules restrict entry screening, gender-congruent government facilities, and passport/visa marker treatment; state law bans congruent restrooms or changing rooms in government buildings including airports, and creates criminal trespass, evidenced by arrest and wrong-ward custody. Immigration-custody abuse reports, care restrictions, and counterterrorism language increase severity if discovered. Courts and local protections partially mediate but institutions enforce restrictions. No execution or routine long imprisonment is documented, so it is above the severe band, but border, facility, custody, and minor-care exposure make visitor risk high.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal entry screening: trans athletes barred; visa applicants with document or record discrepancies may be refused or asked for evidence; suspected material misrepresentation can support permanent lifetime immigration ineligibility. Governments issued travel advisories; reports of passports blocked or confiscated and travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X markers remain valid only until expiry; home-passport acceptance is not documented as safe. Litigation and advisories signal scrutiny but provide no traveller-facing offset.
entry_documents.interaction: Appearance, document mismatch, ticket name, or records can route a visitor into secondary review, denial, removal, and state facility or ID checks.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented capitol restroom arrest led to a misdemeanor charge and 24 hours in a men ward. Immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, and sexual abuse; corrections policies remove hormones and impose conversion-therapy practices.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The one prosecution was dismissed on standing; some care rules were enjoined. No reliable visitor-specific custody remedy is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility refusal or a visa/fraud inquiry can escalate into state jail or immigration detention, where birth-sex placement and abuse are documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities. State law bars congruent restrooms or changing rooms in state and local buildings, schools, airports, and parks; non-members who refuse to leave may face criminal trespass. Bans are widespread across the country.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses are outside the state ban; some other units and cities protect access, but this division lacks GI public-accommodation and hate-crime coverage.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules operate nationwide; this state adds criminal enforcement at airports and government buildings, overlapping document and screening exposure.

care_services.exposure: State law restricts or bans gender-affirming care for minors and adds barriers for adults, including physician-only and conscience refusals. Federal orders target youth care and funding. A visitor needing medication, continuity, or emergency care may be delayed, outed, or refused.
care_services.protection: Some provisions have been blocked and remain in litigation. No operative traveller-facing care guarantee is documented.
care_services.interaction: Care needs can involve records or medication at checkpoints, and facility or custody rules can worsen emergency or continuity care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism language identifies radically pro-transgender groups as hostile; a justice memo associates radical gender ideology with domestic terrorism. Public opinion supports document restrictions. Police alerted in advance arrested a restroom user; state GI hate-crime coverage is absent.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime and employment rulings cover gender identity; some units and cities provide protections, but these do not restore this state facility or hate-crime coverage.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing encourages police to treat gender expression as suspicion or trespass rather than as protected status, reducing reporting safety.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors may be denied puberty blockers, hormones, or social-transition support and can face facility exclusion. Adults facilitating access may be investigated or prosecuted. Custody-modification and out-of-state agreement provisions could expose guardians.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. Some bans were blocked in litigation, but there is no confirmed traveller-specific minor protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian accompanying a minor can become a subject of care, custody, school, facility, or airport scrutiny, with heightened outing.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans women are reported murdered at a rate near the top of monitored units and labelled Do Not Travel. No general background homicide rate is supplied, so magnitude is uncertain; hostile laws and rhetoric may embolden harassment or assault.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law and some city or county ordinances can assist, but this state statute excludes gender identity and enforcement may conflict with the law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police may enforce facility restrictions instead of protecting trans people; being a visible foreigner can amplify staring, filming, or refusal of service.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Outcomes depend on current federal and state orders. Airport application of facility rules is undocumented; travel advisories may be stale; the statute has never been substantively tested; immigration fraud waivers are uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts dismissed one case and blocked some rules; legal-aid guides and civil-liberties suits exist; national employment and hate-crime protections remain partially available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Short visits limit remedy access, and discretionary frontline enforcement can turn a document mismatch or facility question into denial, charge, or custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A. That anchor involves denial and boarding refusal without custody. Here discovery can also involve criminal trespass in government buildings, documented 24-hour wrong-ward detention, possible permanent immigration ineligibility, and care restrictions.

Slightly above 0.25-C. That anchor features systemic prison placement and routine cross-dressing arrests. Here enforcement is less routine: one arrest was dismissed, and raids are not documented. National facility rules, immigration custody abuse, and entry screening still keep risk high.

Materially below 0.65-A. That anchor has brief questioning followed by apology, compensation, and courts reliably blocking unlawful holding. Here law itself criminalises congruent facility use, courts have not tested the statute, and immigration custody abuse is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The operative exposure is not one isolated statute but an interlocking national and state regime. Border screening and document discrepancies can create exclusion or long-term immigration consequences. Once inside, federal and state facility rules force mismatched restroom or changing-room use in government buildings and airports, with state criminal trespass for refusal. Documented arrest shows that enforcement can produce jail, wrong-ward custody, and humiliation; immigration custody adds abuse. Minors and guardians face care denial and possible intervention. Partial court blocks, private-sector carve-outs, and some local protections limit certainty but do not offset active restrictions. The absence of execution or routine long imprisonment keeps this above severe-risk territory; the universal facility, border, custody, and care exposures justify a high-risk score.
